text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe when the swelling and pain in your right ring finger started and if you recall any specific injury or trigger?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the finger appear deformed or bent at an unusual angle, and are you able to fully straighten and bend it? I also need to know if you are experiencing any numbness or tingling sensations in the fingertip.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed description. To help narrow down the diagnosis, I need to know if you can actively extend the finger at the distal joint, or if it remains stuck in that extended position even when you try to bend it. Also, was there any visible bleeding or a 'jammed' sensation at the time of the injury?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your description of the inability to flex the distal joint and the finger remaining extended, I suspect an injury to the flexor tendon. Can you confirm if you can actively bend the very last segment of your finger, or is it completely stuck straight? Also, is the pain localized specifically at the tip of the finger where the tendon inserts?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, numbness, or tingling in the affected finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: It appears I misinterpreted the clinical picture; the inability to flex the distal joint with the finger resting in extension suggests a flexor tendon rupture, likely the Flexor Digitorum Profundus (FDP), rather than an extensor injury. Can you confirm if you can actively curl just the tip of your right ring finger down towards your palm while keeping the middle joint straight? Also, REQUEST TEST: X-Ray Right Hand.

text: I apologize for the repetition. To clarify the mechanism of injury: was the finger forcibly *extended* while you were trying to flex it, or was it forcibly *flexed* while extended? This distinction is critical to differentiate between a Jersey Finger (FDP avulsion) and a Mallet Finger. REQUEST TEST: Ultrasound Right Hand Flexor Tendon.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal ultrasound is puzzling given your inability to flex the fingertip, which strongly suggests a complete Flexor Digitorum Profundus rupture (Jersey Finger) despite the imaging result.
